passages: An officer pulls out a pistol and fires at a block of ice. It shatters into pieces. Then he fires at a second block, and the bullet bounces right off and zips past the admirals!

Because that's not normal ice. It's frozen with sawdust mixed in. It's World War Two, and German submarines are sinking ships in the middle of the Atlantic, out where planes can't reach. So an inventor named Geoffrey Pyke has a wild idea. Build a floating airfield out of ice!

Everyone says ice will just crack and melt. As the story goes, a block was dropped into Winston Churchill's hot bath, and it barely melted. Then the plan got even bigger. A ship two thousand feet long, with walls forty feet thick!
You see, the sawdust works like the steel bars inside concrete. The wood fibres hold the ice together, so a crack can't spread. Torpedo hole? Just pump in seawater and let it freeze solid!
They actually built a test model on a lake in the Canadian Rockies, kept frozen by a tiny motor. Then the whole project was cancelled, and its remains are still sitting at the bottom of that lake.
